podcast.body: Authored by Lindsey Buckingham, this song explicitly reflected the spite and animosity between former couples during the "Rumours" recording. It peaked at number ten on the Hot 100, becoming the band's first-ever US top ten hit by early April 1977. "After Go Your Own Way peaked at number ten, becoming the band's first ever US top ten hit, Dreams did even better, going all the way to the top of the hot 100 by June."

podcast.body: Written by Lindsey Buckingham, this song reached number 10 on the charts. It was Buckingham's response to Stevie Nicks, featuring lyrics accusing her of "packing up and shacking up" and expressing her "yearning for freedom." "In return, Lindsay wrote the number 10 hit Go Your Own Way about Stevie's own yearning for freedom, accusing her of packing up and shacking up."

podcast.body: Written by Lindsey Buckingham, this song was the first single released from the album *Rumours*. It charted in the top 20 and is ranked number 120 on *Rolling Stone*'s "500 greatest songs of all time." The lyrics overtly addressed the tumultuous personal and romantic conflicts within the band, specifically the dynamic between Buckingham and Stevie Nicks. "Go your own way was actually the first single from rumors and it made it to made it into the top 20 and it's also on that rolling stone list at clocks in at 120."
